description: We’re a group of students interested in space, technology, and building cool things together. We’re excited about the SPHEREx and Planet X challenge because it combines astronomy, data, and software!
summary:
We built a reproducible science pipeline that turns SPHEREx Level 2 observations into data a public sky-exploration app can use. It loads FITS images, handles their full distortion-corrected sky coordinates (TAN-SIP WCS), and cuts out and background-subtracts any chosen sky position. For a test field at RA 151.81°, Dec +2.83°, it aligns three epochs (April 2025, May 2025, May 2026) onto one shared grid, masks the area covered by all three, and runs consistent source detection and aperture photometry on each. Results export as catalogues and integration files for the team’s backend and frontend.

This addresses the challenge by making multi-epoch comparison possible, so anyone can see how the same patch of sky looks at different times. It matters because SPHEREx will survey the whole sky repeatedly, and reliable alignment is the first step to spotting change. We also state our limits openly: no wavelength matching, calibration or confirmed classifications yet, so nothing is presented as a confirmed discovery.
details: We built a python pipeline that aligns three SPHEREx observations ( April 2025, May 2025, and May 2026) onto one shared sky grid and runs consistent source detection and photometry on each. This lets anyone explore and compare how same patch of sky looks over time and gives our app reliable data. We used Python, Astropy, photutils and re-project, and we state every limitation openly (results are preliminary and not confirmed discoveries).
